answer: An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the garden index resolves every citation against the quartz checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the meadow audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 149 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 149 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 26 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
